title: Annotatio I §.III (d): Cup is the New Testament in Christ’s blood — many tropes; Valencia / Cajetan
pass_a_gloss: Finally (d) When in the other part of the Institution of the Sacred Supper the proposition occurs, both first uttered by Christ in Luke 22:20 and repeated by the Apostle in 1 Cor. 11:25: The Cup is the N.T. in the blood of Christ — no one will easily deny that it breathes several tropes in one, not even the Pontifician Cajetan on Luke 22 from Thomas Aquinas on 1 Cor. 10; nay rather Gregory of Valencia will also acknowledge the necessity of a trope concerning the Eucharist, Book I ch. 9 th. 42, writing thus: In the proposition This cup is the N.T. in my blood, the cup must altogether be taken for the contained thing, which is Christ’s Blood; and consequently testament or promise is predicated of this blood only figuratively, inasmuch as it confirms the promise and Testament — as that mode of speaking of Matthew and Mark explains in the oblique case, blood of the New Testament.
pass_b_english: (d) In the other half of the Supper Institution — Luke 22:20 and 1 Cor. 11:25 — The Cup is the N.T. in Christ’s blood.
No one easily denies that one line breathes several tropes — not even Cajetan.

Gregory of Valencia grants the necessity: the cup must be taken for the contained blood, and testament/promise is predicated of that blood only figuratively (as Matthew and Mark’s blood of the New Testament shows).
source_text: Denique (d) Cùm in Institutionis S. Coenae parte altera propositio, tùm à Christo primum enunciata, apud Lucam cap. 22. vers. 20. tùm ab Apostolo 1. Cor. 11. vers. 25. repetita, occurrit: Poculum est N. T. in sanguine Christi, unô eam plures tropos spirare nemo facilè inficias ibit, ne quidem Pontificius Cajetanus in Luc. 22. ex Thoma de Aquino 1. Cor. 10.; quin potius Gregorius de Valencia etiam necessitatem tropi agnoscet de Eucharistia Libro I. cap. 9. th. 42. ita scribens: In propositione, Hic calix est N. T. in sanguine meo, oportere prorsus calicem accipi pro re contenta, quae est Christi Sanguis; & consequenter, de hoc sanguine testamentum, seu promissionem, non nisi figurate praedicari, quatenus promissionem videl. & Testamentum confirmat, ut explicat ille dicendi modus Matthaei & Marci in casu nominis obliquo, sanguis Novi Testamenti.

lemmas.gloss: Cup is N.T. in Christ’s blood
